macro.headline: Bull-regime tape cracking under dollar surge and commodity rout — defensives lead.
macro.story:
The headline indices remain above their 50- and 200-day moving averages, but underneath the surface this is a tape in transition, not a clean bull. SPY is roughly 7% above its 200-day but momentum has rolled over: MACD is below signal, RSI has slipped to the mid-40s, and the 5-day move is down about 2.6%. The Dow and Russell are still holding bullish momentum readings (RSI near 59, MACD positive), but the Nasdaq has gone sideways and QQQ printed a sharp -3.3% single-day drop with MACD flipping bearish. That is the classic signature of a leadership handoff away from mega-cap tech, not a broad melt-up.

The dominant cross-asset catalyst, grounded in the active themes, is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle in its CHASING stage colliding with a Geopolitical Risk Unwind in crude. Capital had been concentrated into the AI compute stack while precious metals and energy were being treated as funding sources; this week that trade is digesting. Gold is down ~10% over 21 days with RSI near 31, silver is down ~22% and oversold extended, WTI is down ~27% with RSI at 26, and the DXY is overbought extended at RSI 77.2 — a validated dollar-strength → commodity-headwind setup that is fully expressing itself. The 10Y–2Y curve is flattening hard (spread down ~60% over 21 days, RSI 23) as the front end repricies, which tightens financial conditions even as long yields ease.

Volatility is the tell. Spot VIX at 18.87 is up ~15% in 5 days and ~14% in 21, and is now above its 50- and 200-day with a bullish MACD. That is not a panic reading, but it is a regime where dispersion is rising and the easy beta trade is gone. Engine C's state machine reads CALM — SPY RSI is 46.9, well above any washout threshold — so the validated RSI<30 + above-200 + breadth-thrust bounce setup is NOT active. Do not cite it.

Net: stance is NEUTRAL with LOW confidence because the structural conflict is real — price still above SMAs, but MACD bearish across SPY/QQQ/Nasdaq, VIX rising, DXY parabolic, commodities crashing, and the curve flattening. Hunt longs in sectors with their own internal tailwinds (Financials, Industrials, Utilities); do not lean on index-level beta.

active.name: AI Infrastructure Build-Out — Mega-Cap Compute & Software
active.thesis: Institutional capital is concentrating into the AI compute stack — silicon (NVDA, INTC), infrastructure software (MSFT, PLTR), and the platform/ad layer monetizing inference (META, AAPL). With VIX at 15.88, bullish put/call, and SPY above 50SMA, the TRANSITIONAL regime is being expressed through quality mega-cap tech rather than broad risk-on, suggesting capital is rotating UP the quality curve rather than out.
active.evidence: XLK accel_ratio 1.715 and QQQ accel_ratio 3.323 (14d bull rate 3.3x the 60d baseline) show genuine fresh acceleration, not just persistence. Software-Infrastructure (1.992) and Consumer Electronics (2.246) are leading the doubling-up.

active.name: Natural Gas Reversal — Early Commodity Flip
active.thesis: Natural gas has flipped from ACCELERATING_BEARISH to bullish (+0.37%/day 14d) while crude oil and broader energy commodities (USO, BNO, DBC) are flipping the other way — a divergence that historically signals supply-side gas tightening (storage draw, weather, or LNG export demand) independent of macro oil weakness. Early-stage and contrarian to the broader commodity tape.
active.evidence: UNG is the ONLY commodity in the universe with a bearish-to-bullish flip; every other energy and ag commodity is rolling over. The asymmetry is the signal — but 60d base is still -9.96%, so this is an inflection trade, not a confirmed trend.

invalidators.condition: UNG trajectory returns to DIRECTION_FLIP_bullish_to_bearish or ACCELERATING_BEARISH
EIA weekly storage report prints materially above estimates (bearish surprise)
14d rate decelerates below +0.15%/day for 5 consecutive sessions

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
active.evidence: WTI crude ~$80 (-~5% from recent highs); crude trajectory shifting from HOLDING_BULLISH toward FADING_BULLISH/bearish. Natural gas divergence intact (independent supply story — not demand-driven). Broad commodity complex already fading (DBC, USO, BNO).

invalidators.condition: Iran deal collapses or Hormuz incidents resume — crude reverses sharply higher
OPEC+ emergency production cut to defend $80 floor offsets supply increase
